data.narrative: The student demonstrated exceptional mastery of multi-tenancy, authentication boundaries, and defensive authorization in Module 04. They designed a production-grade API key architecture with SHA-256 hashed persistence, enforced zero-trust tenant isolation with 404 anti-IDOR masking, implemented dual-tier sliding-window rate limiting, and flawlessly diagnosed and remediated an IDOR vulnerability during the incident triage phase.

dimension_scores.observation: Analyzed API Key vs JWT for B2B SaaS, articulating why instant atomic revocation in the database outweighs stateless JWT advantages when enterprise credentials leak.
dimension_scores.evidence: Chose Option A (API Key) citing server-to-server integration simplicity and immediate revocation capability without token blocklists.

dimension_scores.observation: Accurately diagnosed the IDOR root cause to missing query-level tenant predicates in findUnique vs findFirst without any hints, proposing grep/Select-String as the fastest isolation test.
dimension_scores.evidence: Hypothesized that findUnique queried by primary key alone, dropping tenantId scoping, and cited Select-String on prisma.link calls as the fastest check.

dimension_scores.observation: Emphasized that UUID/CUID randomness is security through obscurity, championed 404 Not Found over 403 to prevent IDOR existence probing, and enforced SHA-256 key hashing at rest.
dimension_scores.evidence: Explained how 403 confirms resource existence to attackers, whereas 404 with where: { id, tenantId } shuts down IDOR enumeration completely.

dimension_scores.observation: Designed a zero-downtime overlapping key rotation workflow and instituted dual-tier rate limiting to isolate noisy tenants while protecting unauthenticated public redirects.
dimension_scores.evidence: Outlined multi-key active overlap for credential rotation and configured 30 req/min per tenant on writes vs 120 req/min per IP on redirects.

dimension_scores.observation: Articulated the subtle difference between authentication (401) and authorization (404), providing crisp analogies and RFC-grounded reasoning.
dimension_scores.evidence: Explained authentication ('Who are you?') vs authorization ('Are you allowed to touch this?') with precision and structured production insights.

strengths: Exceptional security awareness regarding IDOR vulnerabilities, resource existence enumeration (404 vs 403), and zero-trust data scoping.
Disciplined root-cause isolation separating the authentication perimeter (auth middleware) from the data isolation layer (Prisma query scoping).
Practical production understanding of zero-downtime credential rotation and dual-tier rate limiting.
growth_areas: Apply this same defensive rigor to caching layers in Module 05, ensuring cached objects maintain tenant isolation and do not leak cross-tenant state.
data.recommendation: Carry forward this zero-trust tenant isolation discipline when designing Redis key namespacing and cache eviction in Module 05.

public_evidence.student_action: Architected API key authentication middleware supporting X-API-Key and Authorization Bearer headers with SHA-256 hashed lookup.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Implemented requireAuth in auth.middleware.ts, resolving API key hash against Prisma ApiKey model, checking revocation, and binding req.tenantId.
public_evidence.proof: Regression test suite confirmed HTTP 401 on missing/invalid keys and HTTP 200 on valid tenant keys (recorded in auth-verification.txt).
public_evidence.ability: Architects secure API authentication perimeters and multi-tenant request contexts
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows deep understanding of API credential security, hashing at rest, and request scoping.

public_evidence.artifact: Anti-IDOR Data Layer & Dual-Tier Rate Limiting
public_evidence.student_action: Enforced tenantId query scoping on all link retrieval endpoints and implemented dual-tier sliding window rate limits.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Used findFirst with { id, tenantId } to return 404 on cross-tenant requests; built rate-limit.middleware.ts enforcing 30 req/min per tenant on writes and 120 req/min per IP on public redirects.
public_evidence.proof: verify-module-04.ts proved Tenant B receives 404 Not Found when requesting Tenant A's link, and verified HTTP 429 throttling on burst requests.
public_evidence.ability: Implements robust multi-tenant authorization defenses and prevents API abuse
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates production-ready defense against IDOR data leaks and DDoS/scraping attacks.
